criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The mission goal, objectives, and quantitative requirements are clearly defined and directly linked to identified Australian stakeholders (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM). The rationale is supported by literature citations.

evidence.quote: Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef, so that bleaching is detected within days

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: A detailed Gantt chart and task narrative are provided, logically ordered around orbital and payload constraints. Thorough risk management with triggers and contingency actions is articulated alongside planned information sources.

evidence.quote: Project work is divided into weeks in the Gantt chart in Figure 1, and each task is described below it.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Includes accurate preliminary orbital hand calculations (period, sun-synchronous inclination, ground-track shift, and swath width). The student critically interprets these findings against revisit requirements to identify a key design trade.

evidence.quote: the reef is up to about 250 km wide, so a 60 km swath needs at least five neighbouring passes to cover its widest part

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report is structured logically with excellent grammar, professional formatting, and clear figures and tables. In-text citations and reference list entries adhere consistently to IEEE standards.

overall: An exemplary preliminary report. The mission concept is well motivated, the project plan is robust with thoughtful contingencies, and the preliminary orbital calculations are technically sound and effectively interpreted.

feedback.summary: You have delivered an exemplary preliminary report. Your mission concept in 'Mission Concept & Rationale' is thoroughly motivated and clearly connected to Australian stakeholders. Furthermore, your 'Project Plan' presents a robust schedule with thoughtful contingencies, and your orbital hand calculations in 'Preliminary Progress' demonstrate strong technical competence. Maintain this high standard of technical rigor and clear documentation as you advance into the full mission design.
next_steps: Progress your orbital calculations from 'Preliminary Progress' into detailed simulations to resolve the swath width versus revisit rate design trade.
Expand your high-level user requirements into quantitative, verifiable subsystem performance specifications and budgets (mass, power, data).
Track task execution against your Figure 1 Gantt chart and document how any triggered contingencies influence your final architecture.

criteria.C1: In 'Mission Concept & Rationale', you clearly defined quantitative goals and linked them effectively to Australian stakeholders like GBRMPA and AIMS with strong literature support. To maintain this Accomplished level in the final report, continue tracing these high-level user needs directly down into specific, verifiable subsystem and payload requirements.
criteria.C2: Your 'Project Plan', centered around Figure 1's Gantt chart and detailed task descriptions, achieved an Accomplished rating through robust risk triggers and contingency actions. To retain this level for the final mission assignment, document your execution against these milestones and explain how your planned information sources supported your design decisions.
criteria.C3: In 'Preliminary Progress', you provided accurate preliminary orbital calculations and critically evaluated the 60 km swath against reef coverage requirements. To maintain the Accomplished level, build upon these initial findings by conducting detailed payload trade studies and orbit simulations to confirm your constellation or revisit strategy.
criteria.C4: Your report met the Accomplished standard with a logical structure, professional formatting, and consistent IEEE referencing throughout. Keep this standard in your final report by ensuring any new subsystem figures, data tables, and expanded reference lists maintain the same high level of clarity and consistent styling.
